title: Halftime Teasers
desc: Rules nobody reads, bizarre records & the stories behind the stats

questions.q: A regulation golf ball has how many dimples, roughly?
In the entire history of the modern Olympics, which country has won the most total medals?
What sport was played on the Moon, and who played it?
questions.a: Golf — Alan Shepard hit two balls during Apollo 14 in 1971

questions.q: A standard dartboard is divided into how many numbered sections?
In football, the 'Cruyff Turn' is named after Johan Cruyff — but in which World Cup did he first perform it on the world stage?
questions.a: 1974 World Cup in West Germany (Netherlands vs Sweden)

questions.q: How many feathers are in a regulation badminton shuttlecock?
questions.a: 16 feathers (always from the left wing of a goose)

questions.q: The fastest serve ever recorded in tennis was clocked at roughly what speed?
questions.a: About 263 km/h (163 mph) — by Sam Groth in 2012

questions.q: In sumo wrestling, what happens if both wrestlers touch the ground at exactly the same time?
questions.a: The heavier wrestler loses — it's called a 'simultaneous fall' and weight is the tiebreaker

questions.q: Which team sport has the largest pitch by area?
questions.a: Polo — a full-size polo field is roughly 300 yards long

questions.q: The Olympic rings represent what — the five continents, the five original sports, or something else?
questions.a: The five continents (Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania) — with colours chosen because every nation's flag contains at least one of them
